security_spec.violation_condition: In a Linux KVM hypervisor on RISC-V with Smctr, if KVM does not trap and emulate vsctrctl (0x24E/0x14E) accesses, a guest VM in VS-mode can write to vsctrctl fields that alias directly to mctrctl bits, thereby modifying M-mode CTR configuration (e.g., enabling M-mode recording via bit 2, toggling freeze-on-breakpoint, or changing inhibit masks) from within a less-privileged virtualized context. The aliasing architecture (vsctrctl → mctrctl) means the guest write propagates to the same physical hardware register bits used by M-mode firmware and the host.
security_spec.summary: vsctrctl fields alias to mctrctl without hypervisor mediation; guests can escape VS-mode to manipulate M-mode CTR recording, violating privilege isolation and potentially leaking or corrupting control-flow traces across security domains
